bug: The first parity thresholds (DOM 0.99, style 2%, pixels 1%) let a planted defect through: the page title recoloured to red scored DOM 0.9986, style 0.34%, pixels 0.07% and the gate passed.
caught_by: parity --selftest, which plants three defects on the original and requires the gate to fail on each
fix: Measured the noise floor (original against itself: DOM 1, style 0, pixels 0) and set thresholds to DOM 1, style 0, pixels 0.05%. The self-test now requires every planted defect to fail the gate.

bug: The scaffold command installed dev dependencies with output sent to /dev/null. npm had failed with ERESOLVE (typescript 7.0.2 against typescript-eslint's peer range below 6.1), so no compiler, bundler or linter was installed, and the script went on to report success.
caught_by: The first parity run against the dev server: page.goto failed with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED and the scenario scored DOM 0, which the gate treats as a failure, not as a skipped check
fix: Pinned typescript to 6.0 inside the linter's supported range; install output is no longer discarded.

bug: The harness hid the replica notice with CSS for the pixel check but still walked it in the DOM check, so every scenario carried one extra line and none could reach the required DOM score of 1 (kalshi_d: 0.9974 with style 0 and pixels 0).
caught_by: The page builder's parity runs: 44 of 44 scenarios failed with an identical one-line DOM difference, the notice itself
fix: The DOM walk skips the notice element, matching the declared waiver.

bug: The scaffold installed the newest lucide-react (1.72) and recharts (3.10.1). The original runs lucide-react 0.453.0 and recharts 3.7.0: the moon icon's path differs, and the newer chart library names its layers, wraps each line in an extra group and drops a tooltip transition (battle_d: DOM 0.8595, 31 differing lines).
caught_by: Parity DOM diff on the theme toggle and on every chart; confirmed by rerunning the scenarios against the older versions
fix: Pinned both libraries to the versions the original's bundle contains.

bug: The dev proxy was keyed on the prefix /api, which also matches the page route /api-docs, so the dev server returned the original's HTML for that page instead of the replica (apidocs_d: DOM 0, style 1, pixels 0.131).
caught_by: Parity on the api-docs scenarios: 48 DOM lines against 224 and every click step timing out
fix: The proxy key is anchored to /api/ so only API calls are forwarded.

bug: In dev and preview the proxy forwarded every method upstream, so submitting the replica's form outside the harness would have posted a real entry to the original's server. Only the production function answered writes locally.
caught_by: A builder reading the config while writing the submit scenarios; no check covered it because the harness intercepts POST before the dev server sees it
fix: The dev proxy answers every non-GET request locally. A check was added: a POST to the running dev server must come back marked as answered by the replica.

bug: The pixel check was not repeatable on one page: polymarket_d scored 0.0005 (pass) and 0.0006 (fail) on consecutive runs with DOM and style equal. One trader's avatar is an animated GIF (96 frames), so each screenshot caught a different frame on both sites.
caught_by: Three reruns of the same scenario giving different results; sampling the image five times through the harness showed its hash changing on both sites
fix: The harness serves both sites a single still pixel in place of any animated GIF (declared waiver W2).

bug: On the first run of a scenario, the two sites asked for the same new image at the same moment and the harness fetched it twice; one site could paint before its copy arrived and show a blank avatar. A second run passed.
caught_by: A dozen scenarios failing on pixels in a first full run and passing unchanged on rerun
fix: The harness shares the in-flight request between the two sites, so both get the same response at the same time.

bug: The API layer forwarded any query string upstream (each new parameter value was a new cache entry and a new upstream request), forwarded the visitor's Accept header while caching on the URL alone, passed any upstream content type through, and admitted single-dot path segments that URL building then folded away (kalshi/./history was fetched as kalshi/history). The handler itself had no test, and the allowlist coverage test read a git-ignored folder and skipped when it was empty, so in CI it could never fail.
caught_by: An independent code review by a reader given only the code, findings 3, 4, 5 and 9, each confirmed by reading
fix: Each route lists its own query parameters and anything else is a 400 before upstream is called; the Accept header is fixed; only JSON and image responses under a size cap are served; dot segments are refused; ten handler tests run against a stubbed upstream; the coverage test reads a committed list the gate regenerates and fails on an empty list.

bug: While hardening the allowlist, the pattern for a name was changed to forbid a leading dot. Two real Kalshi usernames in the recorded data start with a dot (.KJ. and .bananafish), so their avatars would have returned 404 in production.
caught_by: The allowlist coverage test, on its first run against the 629 recorded API calls: it listed the two refused paths
fix: Names may start with a dot; a segment that is only dots is still refused by the segment check.

bug: Two defects in the deploy checks, both seen on the first live deploy. The cache check looked for an s-maxage directive in the response header, which the host consumes and strips, so it failed on a site whose cache was working (second request: x-vercel-cache HIT, age 18). And the deploy script took the last line of the deploy command's output as the URL; the command printed JSON, so the recorded URL was a closing brace.
caught_by: The live API contract run printed FAIL 23/24 on the cache check, and the deploy script printed deployed: }
fix: The cache check makes two requests and requires the second to be served from the edge cache. The script extracts the deployment URL by pattern and stops if there is none.
